abstract: The choroid plexus (CP) produces cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and resides at the interface between CSF and circulating blood. How the CP establishes permeable endothelial identities and properties distinct from neighboring barrier-forming endothelium remains unknown. By developing new genetic and functional screening platforms in zebrafish, we identified blood flow-responsive KLF2 orthologues, klf2a and klf2b, as critical regulators of CP endothelial identity and permeability. Subsequent investigations linked these findings to hemodynamic and mechanosensitive Yap1/Wwtr1 signaling requirements. Expression analyses showed Yap1/Wwtr1 in endothelial and epithelial CP compartments, while epistatic analyses suggested that Yap1/Wwtr1 activity counteracts reduced hemodynamic inputs in the endothelium. Conversely, Yap1/Wwtr1 activity regulates epithelial expression of the VEGFA orthologue vegfab, which signals through endothelial Vegfr2 in CP vascular specialization. These findings define hemodynamic and Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent epithelial-endothelial signaling as crucial determinants of CP vascular specialization and propose that systemic and organ-specific fluid mechanics intersect to shape tissue environments generating unique cellular properties.
